title: devx-sdk-todo-2026-03-04-v4
content:
Daily scratchpad - SDK docs / sample app fixes (rough notes)
Owner: Samantha Lee
Date: 2026-03-04

Context: cleaning up quickstart, samples, and a few doc gaps called out by support + first-time users. Priorities: make quickstart runnable in <10 minutes, add streaming + function-calls examples, and fix auth snippets that confuse people using Hosted API vs Dedicated.

Top priorities (today)
- [ ] Quickstart: Node + Python examples sync (ensure both use same model name + auth pattern).
    - Action: update Node snippet to use fetch + streaming example (handle server-sent events).
    - Blocker: confirm hosted API path (conversation with infra needed) -> pinged devon.
- [ ] Add function-calling example to "chat" sample app (JS + Py).
    - Note: show when to use `tools` vs function schema; include simple reservation example.
- [ ] Streaming docs: show incremental token handling in Python SDK (async iterator) + Node SSE.
    - Add a tiny test harness in samples to validate behavior.
- [ ] Embeddings guide: clarify when to use batch embeddings vs single-call; add snippet for batching with backoff.
- [ ] Update rate-limiting section in quickstart: show 429 handling + retry-after header use.

Smaller fixes / nice-to-have
- Fix typo in "model catalog" page: "quantization-freindly" -> "quantization-friendly".
- Add troubleshooting note: "If you see consistent 503s on Dedicated, check model pin + region routing" (link to ops runbook).
- Sample app: "chat-with-memories" - fix persistence example (was using localStorage incorrectly for SSR).
- Add Node 20 compatibility note for sample apps (some deps break on older node).

Technical notes / snippets to include
- Quickstart auth note: for Hosted API show: `Authorization: Bearer <REDWOOD_API_KEY>` and for Dedicated/private callout on KMS keys and host override.
- Streaming (Node) minimal example: show fetch + ReadableStream reader, handle partial JSON lines -> include fallback to chunked plain text.
- Function calling (Python): include typed dataclass for parsed args + example of fallback when tool not found.

Open questions / blockers
- Confirm default model in quickstart: should we point to `redwood/fast-chat-1` or a curated open model (ask product).
- Does infra want us to show autoscaling config snippet in Dedicated docs (probably not - ops only).
- Who signs off on function-calling wording? Evan suggested stricter language to avoid users overloading tools.

Reviewers / owners for each change
- Quickstart sync: Samantha -> reviewer Evan Brooks (devx lead)
- Streaming + function-calling examples: Samantha + Devon for runtime correctness
- Embeddings batching: Priya (applied-ml) for recommended batch sizes

Deliverables & timeline (tentative)
- Quickstart update + tests: draft by 2026-03-06, review 03-07
- Streaming + function-calls: snippets in repo PR by 2026-03-09
- Embeddings doc updates: 2026-03-10

Draft PR checklist (for myself)
- [ ] Update docs/quickstart.md + include runnable codeblock for Node/Py
- [ ] Add tests in samples/quickstart to assert basic request/response flows (CI friendly)
- [ ] Link to GH PRs in the Confluence page and add a short changelog entry
- [ ] Run through fresh account onboarding flow to verify steps (use staging API key)

Notes-to-self (random)
- When writing sample code, keep everything under 30 lines where possible. People copy-paste.
- Add comments in samples about costs (embedding vs text gen) to prevent surprise bills.
- Remember to mention `streaming: true` option in both SDKs (some customers didn't notice it exists).

Useful links
- GH sample app: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/tree/main/samples/quickstart
- Reported issue: GH PR #412 (missing streaming example)
- Internal ticket: RDW-1023 (docs gaps from onboarding)

Next steps (today)
1) Update quickstart Node snippet -> push small PR, mention Evan for review.
2) Draft streaming example in Python (async generator), add to samples.
3) Reach out to Priya for embeddings batch guidance.

-- end of scratchpad --
(rough, will clean before PR but keeping action items concise)
